pois.name: Car Rental in Gran Canaria
pois.shortDescription: Compare car rental prices in Gran Canaria and save up to 70% with the best providers.
pois.description:
Getting around Gran Canaria by car is the most free and comfortable way to explore the island: from the Maspalomas dunes to Roque Nublo, from the interior ravines to the coastal villages. With over **70 km of motorway** and well-signposted roads, it is a perfect island for road trips.

### Why rent a car?
- 🚗 Access to places without public transport (Güi-Güi, Veneguera, Tasarte)
- 🗺️ Total freedom of schedules and stops
- ⛽ Cheaper petrol than mainland Spain (IGIC fuel tax at 0%)
- 🌡️ Stable climate all year round — great for convertibles
- 💶 Very competitive prices, especially outside peak season

### Practical tips
**Airport pickup:** Most companies have a counter at Gran Canaria Airport (LPA). Book in advance during peak season (December–January and July–August).

**Insurance:** We recommend taking **Full Coverage** (included in the search engine) to avoid surprises with the excess.

**What type of car to choose:**
- Coastal roads and motorways → small hatchback (Seat Ibiza, VW Polo)
- Interior and ravines → crossover or SUV (Seat Arona, Dacia Duster)
- Group of 4-5 people → compact or estate

### Best road trips
From Las Palmas, the **GC-1 South Road** offers ocean views down to Maspalomas. The **GC-60** crossing the centre is one of the most spectacular roads in Spain. The detour to **Tejeda and Artenara** is a must.

Use the search engine to compare prices between Hertz, Sixt, Europcar, Goldcar, ClickRent and over 50 local and international providers.

pois.shortDescription: Gran Canaria's intercity bus network with 129 lines connecting the whole island, from the airport to the south.
pois.description:
**Guagua Global** is Gran Canaria's intercity public transport operator. With **129 lines** and over **2,500 stops**, it covers virtually the entire island at very affordable prices.

### Key lines for tourists
- 🛫 **Line 60** — Airport (LPA) ↔ Las Palmas de Gran Canaria
- 🌅 **Line 66** — Airport (LPA) ↔ Faro de Maspalomas
- 🏖️ **Line 30** — Las Palmas ↔ Playa del Inglés / Maspalomas
- 🌊 **Line 91** — Playa del Cura ↔ Las Palmas
- 🏔️ **Line 18** — Las Palmas ↔ Tejeda (interior)

### Fares and payment
- 💶 Single ticket: **~€1.40** (pay by bank card or app)
- 📱 Contactless bank card payment accepted directly on the bus
- 🎟️ Multi-trip passes available on the website and app

### Practical tips
**From the airport:** Line 60 goes to the centre of Las Palmas and Line 66 connects directly to Maspalomas — ideal if you're staying in the south without needing a taxi.

**App and real-time info:** Download the Guagua Global app to check real-time schedules, plan routes and buy tickets online.

**Main station:** San Telmo Bus Station (Las Palmas) is the central hub where most intercity lines connect.

🌐 More info and timetables at [guaguasglobal.com](https://guaguasglobal.com)

pois.name: Barranco de Guayadeque
pois.description:
One of the most iconic ravines in Gran Canaria, **Guayadeque Ravine** has been inhabited since pre-Hispanic times and is now protected as a Special Area of Conservation. Its dramatic landscape of volcanic cliffs, cave dwellings and fertile terraces makes it one of the island's most fascinating natural and cultural destinations.

### The Trail
Follow the ravine upstream through a landscape of **ancient cave homes**, archaeological sites, terraced fields and subtropical vegetation. As the route climbs towards the highlands, spectacular views open up across one of the most historic and scenic valleys in Gran Canaria.

### Before You Go
- 📍 The route is **not signposted**, so download a GPS track before starting
- ⚠️ Several junctions can be confusing along the way
- 👟 Wear suitable footwear and bring enough water
- 📸 The ravine offers excellent opportunities for landscape and cultural photography


### ⚠️ Safety alerts
- 🌦️ **Changeable weather**: conditions in Gran Canaria can shift rapidly, especially on summits and in ravines — check the AEMET forecast before setting out
- 📵 **No mobile signal** in most ravines and inland natural spaces — download the route offline before you go
- 💧 **Hydration**: always carry more water than you think you need; most trails have no water sources
- 🥾 **Appropriate footwear**: volcanic terrain can be uneven and very slippery after rain
- ☀️ **Intense sun**: use SPF 50+ even on cloudy days — latitude and altitude amplify UV exposure significantly
- ⚠️ **Stay on marked paths**: ravine zones can have rockfall and unstable ground off-trail
- **Emergencies: 112**

### Recommendation
The famous **cave restaurants** are a must-visit stop, offering traditional Canarian cuisine served inside volcanic caves carved into the rock.

Its most distinctive feature is La Barra, a natural reef that protects much of the beach and creates a sheltered lagoon with calm waters, ideal for swimming, snorkelling and enjoying the ocean with the family. Along the promenade you'll find cafés, restaurants and a vibrant atmosphere throughout the year.

- 🏖️ Ideal for families, swimmers and snorkelling enthusiasts

- 🍽️ The promenade offers a wide range of restaurants and local cuisine

pois.name: Gastronomía de Gran Canaria
pois.description:
The cuisine of Gran Canaria is one of the most authentic expressions of the island's identity. Influenced by indigenous traditions, Atlantic heritage and centuries of cultural exchange, it combines high-quality local products with recipes passed down through generations. From the mountain villages to the coastal towns, each area contributes its own flavours, ingredients and specialties that reflect the diversity of Gran Canaria's landscapes.

### What to Try
Among the must-try dishes are **papas arrugadas with mojo sauce**, traditional **gofio**, **Canarian sancocho**, fresh Atlantic fish and a variety of local stews prepared with regional ingredients. Other highlights include the renowned **Flor de Guía Cheese**, unique for its use of vegetable rennet, the famous **Teror chorizo**, traditional soups and stews, and a growing culinary scene that blends Canarian tradition with modern creativity.

### Sweet Flavours
Desserts hold a special place in the island's cuisine. **Bienmesabe**, made from almonds, honey and eggs, is one of the most iconic sweets. Visitors should also try the famous **Suspiros de Moya**, traditional convent pastries and many other handcrafted desserts found in markets and villages across Gran Canaria.

### Unique Local Products
- 🧀 Internationally award-winning artisan cheeses
- ☕ Agaete coffee, one of the few coffees grown in Europe
- 🍷 Volcanic wines produced in different parts of the island
- 🐟 Fresh fish and seafood from the Atlantic Ocean
- 🌴 Tropical fruits grown thanks to Gran Canaria's privileged climate

### Before You Sit Down to Eat
- 🍽️ Look for traditional local restaurants to discover authentic Canarian recipes
- 🐟 Ask about the catch of the day for the freshest seafood experience
- 🧀 Sample different varieties of Canarian cheese, among the most awarded in Spain
- 🛒 Visit local markets to discover regional products and artisan gastronomy

### Recommendation
Exploring Gran Canaria through its cuisine is one of the best ways to discover the island's history, traditions and character. Every dish, ingredient and recipe tells part of the cultural story that has made Gran Canaria one of the most interesting gastronomic destinations in the Canary Islands.

pois.name: Mirador de Unamuno
pois.description:

From this natural balcony, visitors can enjoy outstanding views of the **Tejeda Caldera**, **Roque Nublo** and **Roque Bentayga**, three of the most iconic geological landmarks in the Canary Islands.

### The Visit
The viewpoint is named after the writer and philosopher **Miguel de Unamuno**, who was deeply inspired by the beauty and grandeur of these mountains during his visit to Gran Canaria. From here, visitors can fully appreciate the scale of the island's ravines, volcanic formations and dramatic landscapes that make the interior of Gran Canaria so unique.

- 🌅 Sunrise and sunset provide exceptional photography opportunities

pois.name: Mirador Degollada de las Yeguas
pois.description:

Located between the island's central highlands and the southern coast, it overlooks the vast **Tirajana Ravine**, an extraordinary landscape shaped over millions of years by erosion and volcanic activity. Due to its scale and dramatic relief, many visitors compare it to a miniature Grand Canyon.

### The Visit
From this natural balcony, visitors can admire a landscape dominated by deep ravines, steep slopes and striking rock formations that reveal the island's fascinating geological history. The contrast between the ochre-coloured cliffs, the vegetation of the valley and the changing light throughout the day creates an ever-changing and unforgettable view.

- 📸 One of the best viewpoints in Gran Canaria for panoramic photography
- 🌅 Sunrise and sunset provide particularly spectacular lighting conditions
- 🌬️ Winds can be strong in exposed areas
- 🚗 Easily accessible from the road connecting the central highlands with Maspalomas

### Recommendation
Take a moment to appreciate the scale of the ravine before continuing your journey towards the mountains or the southern coast. It is one of the best places to understand the natural forces that shaped Gran Canaria.

From this remarkable vantage point, visitors can admire a landscape shaped by deep ravines, extensive pine forests and volcanic formations that reveal millions of years of geological history.

The viewpoint overlooks some of Gran Canaria's most iconic landmarks, including **Roque Nublo**, **Roque Bentayga** and the island's central highlands. - 📸 One of the best viewpoints in the Canary Islands for landscape photography
- 🌅 Sunrise and sunset provide exceptional viewing conditions
- 🧥 Bring warm clothing, as temperatures can be significantly cooler than on the coast

The **Cruz de Tejeda Viewpoint** is one of the most iconic landmarks in Gran Canaria's highland region and an unmissable stop for anyone wishing to understand the island's spectacular geography. Located at a historic crossroads used for centuries by travellers and merchants, it offers one of the widest and most recognisable panoramas of the island's mountainous interior.

From this privileged natural balcony, visitors can admire deep ravines, sweeping volcanic slopes and some of the island's most celebrated landmarks, including **Roque Nublo** and **Roque Bentayga**. On the clearest days, the silhouette of **Mount Teide** appears above the Atlantic, completing one of the most iconic views in the Canary Islands.

- 🌅 Sunrise and sunset provide particularly spectacular lighting conditions

pois.name: Parque Rural de Doramas
pois.description:
The **Doramas Rural Park** protects one of the most valuable and distinctive natural environments in Gran Canaria. Located in the island's northern midlands, it preserves some of the last remnants of the ancient **laurel forest**, the subtropical woodland that once covered much of the Canary Islands before the arrival of the first settlers. Its ecological importance makes it one of the best places to experience the rich biodiversity of Gran Canaria.

### The Visit
This extensive protected area is home to lush ravines, natural springs, humid forests and iconic sites such as **Los Tilos de Moya**. Its trails wind through landscapes dominated by laurels, lindens, ferns and other native species, offering a completely different experience from the island's better-known volcanic and coastal scenery.

### Before You Go
- 👟 Trails are available for a variety of hiking abilities
- 🌿 Stay on marked paths to help protect the ecosystem
- 📸 An excellent destination for nature photography and birdwatching
- 🌧️ Some sections may be damp or slippery after rainfall

pois.name: Los Azulejos de Veneguera
pois.description:
**Los Azulejos de Veneguera** form one of the island's most remarkable and distinctive geological landscapes. Its striking shades of green, yellow, red and ochre create a vast multicoloured mountainside that contrasts dramatically with the surrounding volcanic terrain, making it one of the most unusual natural wonders in the Canary Islands.

### The Visit
These formations owe their appearance to ancient volcanic and hydrothermal processes that altered the mineral composition of the rocks over millions of years. The result is a natural mosaic of colours and textures that has made this corner of Veneguera a must-see destination for photographers, geology enthusiasts and anyone interested in unique landscapes.

- 📸 One of the most photogenic locations in Gran Canaria
- ☀️ Bring sun protection, as there is very little shade
- 🚗 Easily visible from the GC-200 scenic road
- 🌅 Early morning and late afternoon light enhance the mountain's colours

pois.name: Barranco de las Vacas
pois.description:
Hidden in the interior of Gran Canaria, the **Barranco de las Vacas** is home to one of the island's most remarkable geological formations. Over thousands of years, water erosion has sculpted a narrow canyon of smooth curves and undulating walls that resembles the famous slot canyons of the American Southwest, making it one of the most photographed locations in Gran Canaria.

- ☀️ There is very little shade, especially during the warmer months

pois.name: Catamaran cruise from Puerto Rico
pois.description:
One of the most popular activities on Gran Canaria's south coast: a **catamaran** cruise from **Puerto Rico** harbour combining dolphin and whale watching in the open Atlantic with a stop to swim and snorkel in crystal-clear waters.

### The experience
During the trip, the boat sails into the **Atlantic Ocean** while guides scan the water for common dolphins, striped dolphins and, with luck, larger cetaceans. The stop at a quiet cove allows you to snorkel in remarkably clear water. Soft drinks are served on board, and some departures include light snacks.

### What to expect
- 🐬 Dolphin spotting with a high success rate
- 🤿 Snorkelling with equipment included in calm waters
- 🛥️ Sun deck and shaded areas on board
- ☀️ Spectacular views of the Mogán cliffs and the southwest coast
- 🥤 Drinks included during the cruise

### Duration and logistics
The excursion lasts approximately **3.5 hours**. Departure is from **Puerto Rico harbour**, well connected with Maspalomas, Playa del Inglés and the rest of the south coast. Arriving early to check in is recommended.

### Is it worth it?
**Yes, especially if you are travelling with children or as a family.** Seeing wild dolphins in their natural habitat is an unforgettable experience, and the combination of snorkelling and coastal scenery makes this one of the most complete activities Gran Canaria has to offer.

### Tips
- 🧴 Apply sunscreen before boarding
- 👟 Wear comfortable footwear and bring swimwear
- 🎒 No previous snorkelling experience required
- 📷 Keep your camera ready from the moment you set sail — dolphins can appear at any time
- 🌊 If you are prone to seasickness, take preventive medication before departure

### Recommendation
Book in advance, especially during high season (July–September), as places fill up quickly. One of the best value-for-money activities in southern Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: Catamaran cruise to spot dolphins, with a snorkel stop near Mogán

pois.name: Off-road buggy adventure in Ayagaures Valley
pois.description:
A different kind of adventure for discovering the interior of **Gran Canaria** behind the wheel of an off-road **buggy**. The route winds along dirt tracks through the **Ayagaures Valley**, one of the most authentic valleys in the south of the island, with views of the reservoir, mountains and landscapes that have nothing in common with the tourist coast.

### The experience
The tour sets off in a guided convoy of buggies from the meeting point in the south of the island. Over **2 hours**, the route crosses canyons, natural viewpoints and dirt tracks that are almost impossible to reach any other way. Local guides explain the geology and history of the valley throughout the trip.

### What to expect
- 🚙 Two-seater buggies that are easy to drive — no licence required for some models
- 🏔️ Unique inland scenery: canyons, reservoir and southern mountains
- 🗺️ Guided convoy tour with a local guide
- 📸 Stops at viewpoints with panoramic vistas
- ⚡ Guaranteed adrenaline on dirt tracks and tight corners

### Duration and logistics
**2-hour** excursion. The departure point is in **southern Gran Canaria**, easily accessible from Maspalomas, Playa del Inglés and the southern resort corridor. Safety equipment is provided.

### Is it worth it?
**Absolutely, especially for those looking for something beyond the beach.** Ayagaures Valley is virtually unknown to mass tourism, guaranteeing an authentic experience far from the most crowded areas.

### Tips
- 👓 Bring sunglasses or protective eyewear — the tracks kick up dust
- 👕 Wear clothes you don't mind getting dirty
- 📷 Keep your camera in a safe spot while driving
- ☀️ Sun protection is essential as there is little shade
- 🚗 Check whether a driving licence is required for the buggy model

### Recommendation
Perfect for couples, groups of friends or families with older children. Combine it with an afternoon on Maspalomas beach or a visit to the Maspalomas Dunes to make the most of your day.
pois.shortDescription: Guided buggy ride through mountain tracks and reservoirs in southern Gran Canaria

pois.name: Submarine Excursion in Puerto de Mogán
pois.description:
One of the most original and accessible experiences in Gran Canaria: a real **submarine excursion** aboard the **Golden Shark (Tiburón Dorado)**, which descends to 25 metres below the surface off Puerto de Mogán — no wetsuit, no diving experience required.

### The experience
The **Tiburón Dorado** is a tourist submarine that lets you explore the Atlantic Ocean floor in comfort, seated and watching through large panoramic windows. During the **40-minute** dive, you'll discover several **wrecks** (deliberately sunk vessels), coral formations and rich marine life while an audioguide available in **9 languages** explains what you're seeing.

### What to expect
- 🦈 Descend to 25 metres with no pressure change and no diving equipment
- 🐠 Atlantic marine life: grouper, rays, moray eels, shoals of fish
- ⚓ Wrecks and artificial reef structures placed on the seabed
- 📺 TV screens for each passenger showing the submarine's manoeuvres
- 🎧 Audioguide in 9 languages: Spanish, English, German, French, Italian, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish and Finnish
- 📸 Take your own photos through the windows throughout the dive

### Duration and logistics
The excursion lasts **40 minutes**. The boarding point is the **Pantalán Dique Sur jetty** in Puerto de Mogán. Redeem your voucher at the boarding area at least **20 minutes before** departure. Gates close 10 minutes before the start. Free pick-up from the southern resort area may be available — contact the provider directly: **0034 928 56 51 08** (Monday–Sunday, 10:00–16:00).

### Is it worth it?
**Yes, especially for families with children.** The activity requires no special skills or physical condition (suitable from age 2), and offers a completely different perspective on the underwater world. Over 4,000 reviews with an average rating of **4.4 out of 5** speak for themselves.

### Tips
- ⏰ Arrive at the jetty well in advance — the pier is longer than it looks from the car park
- 📷 Bring a charged camera or phone to photograph through the windows
- 🎧 Select your audioguide language before the dive begins
- 🧥 The interior of the submarine can be cool — bring a light layer
- 🅿️ The nearest car park is about 15 minutes' walk from the actual boarding point; factor this into your timing

### Recommendation
A perfect activity to combine with a stroll around the charming village of **Puerto de Mogán**, one of the most beautiful in Gran Canaria. Book in advance during high season as places are limited.
pois.shortDescription: Real submarine excursion to 25 metres depth with audioguide in 9 languages off Puerto de Mogán

pois.name: Aqualand Maspalomas — Water Park
pois.description:
The most complete water park in southern Gran Canaria and one of the leading family leisure destinations in the entire archipelago. **Aqualand Maspalomas** features slides of every speed, shape and height, wave pools, lazy rivers and attractions for the little ones, all within a park open **365 days a year** under the Maspalomas sun.

### The experience
From free-fall slides for thrill-seekers to gentle family slides and splash zones for young children, the park offers something for every member of the family. The grounds are well maintained, with spacious relaxation areas, restaurants and shops inside the park.

### What to expect
- 🎢 High-speed and free-fall slides for adrenaline lovers
- 🌊 Artificial wave pools and lazy rivers
- 👨‍👩‍👧 Dedicated children's zones with smaller attractions
- ♿ Wheelchair accessible
- ☀️ Sun loungers and shaded rest areas
- 🍔 Restaurants and picnic areas within the park

### Duration and logistics
Ticket valid for **1 full day**. Open 365 days a year. Located in southern Gran Canaria, well connected to the main tourist areas: Maspalomas, Playa del Inglés, Meloneras and Arguineguín.

### Is it worth it?
**Yes, especially for families with children.** It is the perfect complement to beach days and one of the most popular activities among tourists and locals in the south of the island. The variety of attractions guarantees hours of fun for all ages.

### Tips
- 🧴 Bring high-factor sunscreen — hours spent in and out of water add up quickly
- 👟 Wear water shoes on the park grounds
- 🎒 Leave valuables in the park's lockers
- ⏰ Arrive early in high season to avoid queues at the most popular attractions
- 🏖️ Combine your visit with nearby Maspalomas beach or the dunes to complete the day

### Recommendation
Book your ticket online in advance to skip the box office queue, especially in summer. A full day at Aqualand is one of the best options for families looking for active fun in southern Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: The largest water park in southern Gran Canaria with slides for all ages, open 365 days a year in Maspalomas

pois.name: Poema del Mar — Skip-the-Line Entry
pois.description:
One of the most spectacular aquariums in Europe and the cultural jewel of **Las Palmas de Gran Canaria**. **Poema del Mar** immerses visitors in the biodiversity of the world's oceans through contemporary design installations that recreate tropical water ecosystems, coral reefs, mangroves and the depths of the Atlantic.

### The experience
The journey through **Poema del Mar** is a visual and sensory immersion in the marine world. Its underwater tunnels, panoramic aquariums and interactive exhibits allow you to observe sharks, rays, tropical fish, jellyfish and hundreds of ocean species up close. The space is designed to offer unique perspectives from every angle, creating a memorable experience for all ages.

### What to expect
- 🦈 Sharks, rays and large predators in large-format aquariums
- 🐠 Coral reefs and tropical fish from the Indo-Pacific and Atlantic
- 🌿 Mangrove ecosystem recreations and coastal habitats
- 🔭 360° underwater tunnels
- 🎟️ Skip-the-line entry — direct access to the aquarium
- 📱 Interactive signage and information panels

### Duration and logistics
Ticket valid for **1 full day**. Located at the **Muelle de Santa Catalina**, in the heart of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, with excellent public transport connections and nearby parking areas.

### Is it worth it?
**Absolutely — it is the best-rated attraction in Gran Canaria.** With a score of **4.8 out of 5** across more than 4,000 verified reviews, Poema del Mar is one of the highest-satisfaction activities on the entire island. A must for families and solo travellers alike.

### Tips
- ⏰ Skip-the-line entry is a huge advantage in high season — don't waste time queuing
- 📷 The tunnel zones and panoramic aquariums offer the best photo opportunities
- 🚌 Santa Catalina pier is well connected to the rest of the city
- 🕐 Allow at least 2–3 hours to explore the aquarium at a relaxed pace
- 🍽️ Combine your visit with a stroll through Las Palmas and the port restaurant area

### Recommendation
Suitable for any type of traveller. If you visit Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, **Poema del Mar** is the most highly rated cultural visit in the city. Book online to guarantee direct, queue-free access.
pois.shortDescription: The most spectacular aquarium in Gran Canaria with skip-the-line entry, rated 4.8★ across over 4,000 reviews, at the Santa Catalina pier in Las Palmas

pois.name: Guided Tour and Tasting at Mundo del Plátano
pois.description:
One of the most highly rated cultural and gastronomic experiences in Gran Canaria: a **guided tour of a real banana farm** where you discover the secrets of cultivation, history and the products made from the Canarian banana — one of the most famous and prized in Europe.

### The experience
During the **40-minute** tour, an expert guide explains the life cycle of the banana plant, the different varieties grown in Gran Canaria, traditional farming techniques and the historical importance of banana cultivation to the Canarian economy. The tour ends with a **tasting** of banana-based products: from fresh banana to artisan liqueurs, chocolates and preserves.

### What to expect
- 🍌 Tour of a real, working banana farm in full production
- 🌱 Explanation of Canarian banana varieties and cultivation methods
- 📜 History of the banana in Gran Canaria and its agricultural importance
- 🍫 Tasting of artisan products made from banana
- 🗣️ Guide in Spanish and English
- 👨‍👩‍👧 Suitable for all ages

### Duration and logistics
The tour lasts **40 minutes**. The activity takes place on a farm on the island of Gran Canaria. Comfortable footwear and sun protection are recommended for the outdoor sections of the tour.

### Is it worth it?
**Yes, especially if you are interested in Canarian culture and gastronomy.** Rated **4.8 out of 5** across more than 3,000 verified reviews, it is one of the highest-rated tours in Gran Canaria. Ideal for those who want to discover the island beyond its beaches and scenery.

### Tips
- 👟 Wear comfortable shoes for walking through the farm
- ☀️ Sun protection recommended — part of the tour is outdoors
- 📷 The farm offers wonderful photo opportunities with banana plants heavy with fruit
- 🍌 If you have a banana allergy, check the tasting products in advance
- ⏰ Short tour, easy to combine with other activities on the same day

### Recommendation
An original and authentic visit that connects you to the agricultural history of Gran Canaria. Perfect for curious travellers, food lovers and families with children. Book in advance as places are limited.
pois.shortDescription: 40-minute guided tour of a real banana farm with artisan product tasting, rated 4.8★ across more than 3,000 reviews

pois.name: Parasailing in Puerto Rico de Gran Canaria
pois.description:
One of the most thrilling aerial experiences on the southern coast of Gran Canaria: **parasailing** over the crystal-clear waters of **Puerto Rico**, towed by a speedboat with up to 300 metres of line, taking in panoramic views of the coastline, the mountains, and the open Atlantic.

### The Experience
The flight lasts **10–12 minutes** and is available in two options: a **150-metre line** for a moderate height, or a **300-metre line** for those who want to go higher and enjoy an even more breathtaking perspective. Take-off and landing are both from the boat itself — no need to get wet and no previous experience required.

### What to Expect
- 🪂 10–12 minute flight over the Atlantic Ocean
- 📏 Choice of 150 m or 300 m line height
- 🚤 Dry take-off and landing directly from the boat
- 👥 Small group: maximum 3 participants per flight
- 🏖️ Panoramic views of Puerto Rico, the southern coast, and the mountains
- 🗣️ English and Spanish-speaking crew

### Duration & Logistics
The flight itself lasts **10–12 minutes**. The activity departs from **Puerto Rico Marina**, in the south of Gran Canaria. No prior experience or special fitness level is needed. Suitable for most ages (weight restrictions may apply — check before booking).

### Is It Worth It?
**Absolutely, especially if you're after adrenaline and aerial views.** Rated **4.6 out of 5** across nearly 650 reviews, this is one of the top-rated water activities in the area. The small group (max 3 people) ensures a personal, uncrowded experience.

### Tips
- 📷 Bring a waterproof case for your phone or camera — or trust the crew's photos
- 👕 Wear comfortable, light clothing — no need for swimwear if you prefer to stay dry
- ☀️ Apply sunscreen before boarding
- 🌬️ Activity is weather-dependent; strong winds may lead to cancellation
- ⏰ Total time including boarding and waiting: approximately 30–45 minutes

### Who Is It For?
Perfect for couples, groups of friends, or families with teenagers looking for a dose of excitement and the best aerial views of southern Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: Parasailing over the Atlantic from Puerto Rico marina with panoramic coastal views, 150 m or 300 m line options, max 3 participants per flight

pois.name: Camel Ride Through the Maspalomas Dunes
pois.description:
One of the most iconic experiences in southern Gran Canaria: riding a camel through the legendary **Maspalomas Dunes**, a unique desert landscape in Europe that feels straight out of the Sahara. Led by Sahrawi guides, this 30-minute ride is an unforgettable way to explore one of the most spectacular natural settings in the Canary Islands.

### The Experience
The camels are fitted with **comfortable two-person saddles**, so there's no need to ride directly on the hump. **Sahrawi guides** accompany the entire ride, sharing fascinating facts about the animals and the natural environment. The route winds through golden sand dunes with views stretching out to the Atlantic horizon.

### What's Included
- 🐪 **30-minute camel ride** through the dunes
- 🎫 Insurance included
- 🚌 Hotel pickup and drop-off available
- 🗣️ Guides in Spanish, English, and German

### Not Suitable For
- People with mobility issues or wheelchair users
- People with vertigo
- People weighing more than **100 kg**

### Meeting Point
From **Charca Maspalomas**, follow **Calle Oceania** for about 5 minutes. You'll find the camel station (Camello Safari Duna Oasis) on your right.

### Is It Worth It?
With a rating of **4.4 out of 5** across nearly **4,800 reviews**, this is one of the most popular and best-rated activities in southern Gran Canaria. Travellers consistently praise the excellent care given to the animals, the friendliness of the guides, and the charm of the desert landscape.

### Tips
- ☀️ Bring sunscreen, water, and insect repellent — essentials in the dunes
- 👕 Wear comfortable, breathable clothing; it can get very hot in summer
- 👶 Children under 3 can ride free with a parent
- ⏰ Entry is on a first-come, first-served basis — arrive with some time to spare
- 📍 Signage to the meeting point can be sparse; follow Calle Oceania from Charca Maspalomas

### Who Is It For?
Perfect for families, couples, or any traveller looking for a truly different experience in a landscape that's unique in all of Europe. Pair it with a sunset stroll through the dunes for a perfect afternoon in the south of Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: 30-minute camel ride through the iconic Maspalomas Dunes with Sahrawi guides, two-person saddles and a unique desert landscape unlike anywhere else in Europe

pois.name: NOMAD Dinner Show at Sala Scala
pois.description:
An unforgettable night out: the **NOMAD** show at the legendary **Sala Scala** in Gran Canaria is widely recognised as the best dinner show in Europe. A captivating journey across the three continents that shaped the Canarian identity, brought to life by more than **30 international artists** on stage.

### The Show
Over **3 hours**, live music, dance, acrobatics and state-of-the-art visual effects light up a stage equipped with **20 metres of LED screens** and spectacular lighting. Each number is choreographed to surprise, move and celebrate life from the very first moment — right through to the finale, where the artists join the audience on the floor for a spontaneous after-party.

### What's Included
- 🎭 **3 hours** of live performance with 30+ international artists
- 🍽️ **Km 0 tasting menu** (depending on ticket category) — local produce as the star
- 🎬 20-metre LED screens, special effects and cutting-edge lighting
- ♿ Wheelchair accessible
- 🍷 Drinks not included (reasonably priced at the venue)

### Ticket Options
- **Show only** — enjoy the performance without dinner
- **Dinner + show** — the most popular option: full show + tasting menu
- **Scala VIP** — premium experience with the best seats in the house
- **Show + wine open bar** — dinner, show and wine included
- **New Year's Eve** — special end-of-year edition

### Schedule
**Thursday to Sunday** at **8:00 PM**. Total duration: 3 to 5 hours depending on the package chosen.

### Is It Worth It?
**Absolutely.** Rated **4.7 out of 5** across more than **750 reviews**, travellers consistently praise the quality of the show, the tasting menu and the unique atmosphere of a venue with **over 35 years of history**. It is one of the most celebrated evening experiences in all of Gran Canaria.

### Tips
- 🎟️ Book in advance — sessions fill up quickly, especially in high season and at weekends
- 👗 No strict dress code, but the occasion calls for smart-casual at the least
- 📱 If you film on your phone, the artists interact with the camera — make the most of it!
- 📍 Located in the Maspalomas area, easily accessible from most hotels in the south
- 🚫 Smoking is not permitted inside the venue

### Who Is It For?
Perfect for couples, groups of friends or anyone celebrating a special occasion. The dinner + show option offers the best value and turns the evening into a complete, unforgettable experience.
pois.shortDescription: Europe's best dinner show: 30+ international artists, live music, acrobatics and a km 0 tasting menu at the iconic Sala Scala in Gran Canaria

pois.name: Palmitos Park — Entry Ticket with Dolphin and Bird Shows
pois.description:
Just **10 kilometres from the Maspalomas lighthouse**, **Palmitos Park** is one of the most extraordinary zoo-botanical parks in Europe: a unique combination of botanical garden, zoo, aquarium and live animal shows set within a natural ravine landscape in the south of Gran Canaria.

### What You'll See
The park is home to animals and plants from all 5 continents, including some truly remarkable highlights:

- 🐬 **Dolphinarium** — the park's flagship attraction, with a spectacular exhibition and live performances
- 🦅 **Birds of prey show** — flight display featuring falcons, eagles and vultures
- 🦜 **Exotic bird show** — children can hand-feed parrots and tropical birds
- 🦎 **Reptile house** — including a **Komodo dragon** from the first generation bred in captivity in Europe (up to 3 m long and 90 kg)
- 🐊 **Caiman lake** — spectacled caimans, California slider turtles and the Gran Canaria giant lizard
- 🐒 **Primate island** — talapoin monkeys and other primate species
- 🦔 **Unique animals** — aardvarks, meerkats and wallabies
- 🦋 **Butterfly house** — indoor tropical garden with free-flying butterflies
- 🐠 **Aquarium** — tropical and marine fish exhibition
- 🦔 **Armadillo show** — popular interactive number, especially with younger visitors

### What's Included
- 🎟️ Park entry and access to **all shows** (dolphins, parrots, birds of prey and exotic birds)
- 🚗 Free parking
- 🍽️ Food and drink available inside the park
- ♿ Wheelchair accessible

### Opening Hours
**Last entry at 5:00 PM**. Arriving in the morning is recommended to comfortably fit in all the shows — a full day visit typically takes 4 to 6 hours.

### Is It Worth It?
Rated **4.7 out of 5** across more than **1,600 reviews**, Palmitos Park is one of the highest-rated parks in the Canary Islands. Visitors consistently highlight the dolphin show, the close-up animal interactions and the beauty of the natural setting.

### Tips
- ☀️ Sun protection is essential — much of the park is outdoors
- 👟 Comfortable walking shoes for the paths and terraces
- 🕐 Check the show timetable at the entrance to plan your day and not miss anything
- 🍽️ There is a restaurant and picnic areas inside the park
- 📍 Located in the Barranco de los Palmitos ravine, 10 km from the Maspalomas lighthouse

### Who Is It For?
A perfect day out for families with children, couples or any traveller who wants to combine nature, exotic animals and world-class live shows in a unique setting. Book in advance to guarantee entry.
pois.shortDescription: Unique zoo-botanical park 10 km from Maspalomas with dolphin shows, birds of prey, exotic bird displays, a butterfly house, aquarium and a Komodo dragon

pois.name: Natural Pools of Agaete
pois.description:
Shaped by ancient volcanic lava flows beside **Puerto de las Nieves**, the **Natural Pools of Agaete** are one of the most spectacular spots on Gran Canaria's northern coast to enjoy the ocean. These natural rock pools fill with clear Atlantic water, creating a perfect place to swim while contemplating the force of the sea and the volcanic landscape.

### The visit
This cluster of natural pools offers areas for swimming, sunbathing and watching the Atlantic break against the volcanic rock. The contrast between the black lava, the deep blue ocean and the mountains surrounding Agaete makes it one of the most photogenic corners of the island.

### Before you go
- 🌊 Check sea conditions, especially on days with heavy swell
- 👟 Wear suitable footwear for walking on volcanic rock
- ☀️ Bring sun protection — there is little shade
- 📸 Ideal for coastal photography and sunsets

### Recommendation
Stroll through nearby **Puerto de las Nieves** and enjoy fresh fish by the sea in one of the most charming coastal villages on Gran Canaria.

---

🌿 **Responsible tourism in the Canary Islands**
Canarian ecosystems are unique in the world. Small gestures make a big difference:

- 🚶 Stick to marked trails and don't access restricted areas
- 🗑️ Leave no trace — take back what you bring
- 🐋 Keep your distance from wildlife and don't feed animals
- 🛍️ Shop local and choose products from the islands
- 💧 Save water — in the Canaries it's a scarce resource
- 📵 Keep quiet in natural spaces — other beings live here

*Travelling well is also part of the experience.*
pois.shortDescription: Natural rock pools carved by ancient lava flows, filled with crystal-clear Atlantic water beside Puerto de las Nieves — a spectacular swimming spot on Gran Canaria's north coast.

pois.name: Ferries from Gran Canaria
pois.shortDescription: Two ports, two destinations: from Las Palmas to Tenerife and Fuerteventura, and from Agaete to Tenerife in just 1h30. You can take your car on board.
pois.description:
Gran Canaria has two ports with ferry connections to other islands:

⚓ **Las Palmas Port (Puerto de La Luz)** — The largest in the archipelago. Ferries depart here to **Tenerife** (1h30-2h30) and **Fuerteventura** (2-3h) Multiple sailings daily.

⚓ **Puerto de Las Nieves (Agaete)** — On the northwest coast. Direct ferry to **Tenerife in just 1h30** from here. Perfect if you're staying in the north or want a quick crossing.

🚗 **Travelling with a car?** You can board with your vehicle at both ports. Book ahead — car spaces sell out fast in summer and on long weekends.

💡 Combine Gran Canaria with Tenerife or Fuerteventura in the same trip and explore the archipelago like few tourists do.

pois.name: Romerías of Gran Canaria
pois.shortDescription: The most deeply rooted festive tradition in the Canaries — processions with ox carts, traditional costumes, folk music and local wine
pois.description:
**Romerías** are the most genuine and colourful expression of Canarian cultural identity. Collectively declared a **Festival of National Tourist Interest**, they are festive processions of religious origin that celebrate each municipality's patron saint with a unique mix of popular faith, folklore, gastronomy and community spirit.

### What is a Romería?
The word «romería» comes from «romero» — the pilgrim who walks to Rome. In the Canaries it refers to the popular procession that each town celebrates in honour of its patron saint: a procession of hundreds or thousands of participants in traditional Canarian dress, accompanied by flower-decorated ox carts bearing the best produce of the land, live folk music, and abundant local wine.

### The Elements of a Romería

**🐂 The Carretas (Ox Carts)**
The visual centrepiece of every romería. Wooden carts pulled by oxen, decorated with flowers, fruits, vegetables, embroidery and rural elements. Each carreta represents a team or association competing in beauty and originality. The scent of damp earth, flowers and wine as the carts pass by is unmistakable.

**👗 The Traditional Canarian Costume**
Participants march in regional traditional dress: for women, brightly coloured underskirt (refajo), embroidered blouse, shawl and straw hat with flowers; for men, short wool breeches, white shirt, sash, waistcoat and hat. Each municipality has its own characteristic colours and embroidery patterns.

**🎵 Folk Music**
Folklore groups (cuadrillas) with timples (the small string instrument unique to the Canaries), guitars, lutes and castanets set the pace of the procession. Canarian rhythms — **folía, isa and tajaraste** — play at every romería. Improvised singing (trovos) is another tradition woven through the parades.

**🍷 Wine and Food**
No romería goes without local wine, Canarian cheese, island cured meats and papas arrugadas with mojo. Romerías are also a gastronomic celebration: the participants share everything they carry on the carts with the public and with each other. Canarian hospitality at its fullest.

### The Most Important Romerías in Gran Canaria

- 🌿 **Romería de Teror** — **8 September** · The largest, in honour of the Virgen del Pino, patron saint of Gran Canaria
- 🌾 **Romería de Agüimes** — **May** · One of the most colourful and well-attended in the south
- 🎉 **Romería de Gáldar** — **August** · In the heart of the north, with great historical tradition
- 🌊 **Romería de la Virgen del Carmen** (various coastal municipalities) — **July** · Maritime procession in fishing villages

### Romería vs. Carnival
If the **Las Palmas Carnival** is the festival of irreverence, excess and urban creativity, the romería is its complementary opposite: the festival of the countryside, tradition, rural identity and roots. Two expressions of the same Canarian spirit, both equally passionate.

### The Timple
The **timple** is to Canarian folklore what the flamenco guitar is to Andalusia: a small stringed instrument with a raised soundbox and crystal-clear tone, heard at every romería, parada and Canarian evening gathering. Hearing it live at a romería is to understand something essential about the culture of these islands.

### Tourist Recommendation
If your visit coincides with any romería, do not miss it — it is one of the most visually and sensorially authentic spectacles Gran Canaria offers. Arrive early to watch the carts pass, accept the wine and cheese the participants offer you (it is part of the tradition), and stay for the evening verbena that follows the parade. The official calendar of romerías and festivals is published by the Cabildo de Gran Canaria each year.

---

🌿 **Responsible tourism in the Canary Islands**
Canarian ecosystems are unique in the world. Small gestures make a big difference:

- 🚶 Stick to marked trails and don't access restricted areas
- 🗑️ Leave no trace — take back what you bring
- 🐋 Keep your distance from wildlife and don't feed animals
- 🛍️ Shop local and choose products from the islands
- 💧 Save water — in the Canaries it's a scarce resource
- 📵 Keep quiet in natural spaces — other beings live here

*Travelling well is also part of the experience.*

municipios.name: Agaete
municipios.description:
**Agaete** is one of the most spectacular and authentic municipalities in **Gran Canaria**. Located at the northwestern tip of the island, it combines a beautiful volcanic coastline, a historic fishing village, fertile agricultural valleys and some of the most impressive landscapes in the archipelago. Thanks to its natural, cultural and culinary richness, **Agaete** has become a must-visit for anyone wanting to discover a different side of **Gran Canaria**.

### What to see in Agaete
Among the most notable sights are the picturesque **Puerto de las Nieves**, the famous **Agaete Natural Pools**, the quiet **Agaete Beach** and the spectacular **Agaete Valley**. The **Ermita de las Nieves** chapel, the viewpoints over the northwest coast and the impressive cliffs surrounding this part of the island are also well worth a visit.

### What to do in Agaete
**Agaete** offers activities for all kinds of travelers. You can swim in the natural pools, hike trails through mountains and ravines, visit farms where the famous **Agaete Coffee** is grown, sample local wines or stroll through the lively seafaring atmosphere of **Puerto de las Nieves**. It is also one of the best places in **Gran Canaria** to enjoy sunsets over the Atlantic Ocean.

### Is Agaete worth visiting?
**Without a doubt.** Agaete brings together nature, gastronomy, culture and some of the most impressive landscapes in **Gran Canaria** in a single municipality. Its combination of volcanic coastline, agricultural valley and seafaring tradition offers an experience very different from the better-known tourist areas in the south of the island.

### Tips for your visit
- 🌊 Check sea conditions before swimming in the **Agaete Natural Pools**
- ☀️ Wear sun protection all year round
- 📸 **Puerto de las Nieves** offers some of the best photo opportunities in **Gran Canaria**
- ☕ Don't leave without trying the famous **Agaete Coffee**, one of the few coffees grown in Europe
- 🚗 Take the chance to drive the spectacular road between **Agaete** and **La Aldea de San Nicolás**
- 🍽️ Try the fresh fish at the restaurants by the harbor

### Recommendation
Spend at least a full day discovering **Agaete**. Between **Puerto de las Nieves**, the **Agaete Natural Pools**, the **Agaete Valley** and the impressive landscapes of the northwest coast, you'll find one of the most complete, beautiful and surprising municipalities in **Gran Canaria**.
municipios.shortDescription: Agaete combines the Puerto de las Nieves, natural pools, the Agaete Valley and some of the most spectacular and authentic landscapes in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Agüimes
municipios.description:
**Agüimes** is one of the most charming municipalities in **Gran Canaria**, rich in history and cultural heritage. Located in the southeast of the island, it is home to one of the **best-preserved historic centers in the Canary Islands**, where cobbled streets, traditional squares and elegant historic buildings transport visitors to another era. Its combination of culture, tradition and nature makes it one of the most recommended visits for anyone wanting to discover the authentic essence of the island.

### What to see in Agüimes
The main attraction is the **Historic Center of Agüimes**, declared a **Site of Cultural Interest**, where the impressive **Church of San Sebastián**, numerous urban sculptures and traditional Canarian houses with wooden balconies stand out. Very close by is the spectacular **Guayadeque Ravine**, one of the most important natural and archaeological sites in **Gran Canaria**, famous for its inhabited caves, ancient aboriginal settlements and restaurants carved into the rock.

### What to do in Agüimes
Strolling through the streets of the historic center is a must. You can also explore the **Guayadeque Ravine**, go hiking, discover the archaeological heritage of the ancient Canarians, or enjoy local cuisine at one of the traditional cave restaurants. For photography lovers, the municipality offers some of the most picturesque corners in the southeast of the island.

### Is Agüimes worth visiting?
**Yes, absolutely.** Agüimes offers an experience very different from the beach resort areas. It's an ideal destination for those looking to learn about history, traditional architecture and Canarian culture. Its excellent state of preservation and the proximity of places like **Guayadeque** make it one of the most interesting cultural visits in **Gran Canaria**.

### Tips for your visit
- 👟 Walk through the **historic center** to discover all its corners
- 📸 **Plaza de San Sebastián** and the urban sculptures are perfect for photography
- 🏛️ Visit the **Church of San Sebastián**, one of the most iconic buildings in the municipality
- 🥾 Set aside time to explore the **Guayadeque Ravine**
- 🍽️ Try traditional Canarian cuisine at the famous **cave restaurants**
- ☀️ Wear sun protection if you plan to hike or visit Guayadeque

### Recommendation
Combine a visit to the **Historic Center of Agüimes** with an excursion to the **Guayadeque Ravine**. Few places bring together **history**, **culture**, **archaeology**, **gastronomy** and **nature** in such a balanced way. It's one of the best options for discovering the most authentic and traditional side of **Gran Canaria**.
municipios.shortDescription: Agüimes stands out for its spectacular historic center, the Church of San Sebastián and the Guayadeque Ravine, one of the most iconic spots in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Artenara
municipios.description:
**Artenara** is the highest municipality in **Gran Canaria** and one of the most spectacular destinations for discovering the island's mountainous interior. Surrounded by deep ravines, impressive volcanic formations and some of the most iconic landscapes in the Canary Islands, this small village retains a strong connection to the history and traditions of the island's ancient inhabitants. Its famous **cave houses**, still inhabited today, make Artenara one of the most singular places in the entire archipelago.

### What to see in Artenara
Among its main attractions are the impressive **Mirador de Unamuno**, the **Mirador de la Atalaya**, the traditional **cave houses**, the nearby **Roque Bentayga** and the protected landscapes linked to the **Risco Caído** archaeological complex, declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. From many points in the municipality you'll get spectacular views of **Roque Nublo**, the **Tejeda Caldera** and the peaks of **Gran Canaria**.

### What to do in Artenara
**Artenara** is one of the best destinations in **Gran Canaria** for hiking, enjoying panoramic routes and discovering traditional Canarian culture. Its trails wind through pine forests, ravines and ancient paths used for centuries by the island's inhabitants. It's also worth visiting the **Casas Cueva Ethnographic Museum**, sampling local cuisine and enjoying some of the best viewpoints in the Canary Islands.

### Is Artenara worth visiting?
**Without a doubt.** Artenara offers a completely different experience from the coastal areas. It's an ideal place for those seeking nature, culture, archaeology and some of the most impressive landscapes in **Gran Canaria**. Its views over the mountainous heart of the island are considered among the best in the archipelago.

### Tips for your visit
- 📸 Bring your camera, as you'll find some of the best viewpoints in **Gran Canaria**
- 🧥 Temperatures tend to be cooler than on the coast, so pack warm clothing, especially in winter
- 🍑 If you visit between January and February, don't miss the almond blossom
- 🚗 The access roads are winding; drive carefully
- 🏠 Visit an inhabited cave house to see what life is like in Artenara

### Recommendation
Spend half a day exploring the viewpoints and cave houses of **Artenara** and combine the visit with an excursion to **Roque Bentayga** or **Risco Caído**. It's one of the best ways to discover the mountainous and most authentic heart of **Gran Canaria**.
municipios.shortDescription: Artenara, the highest municipality in Gran Canaria, stands out for its cave houses, the Roque Bentayga and some of the best viewpoints on the island.

municipios.name: Arucas
municipios.description:
**Arucas** is one of the most monumental and elegant municipalities in **Gran Canaria**. Located in the north of the island, it is famous for its impressive **Church of San Juan Bautista**, popularly known as the **Arucas Cathedral**, for its extensive banana plantations and for its close ties to the history of sugar cane. Its combination of architectural heritage, agricultural tradition and volcanic landscapes makes **Arucas** one of the most interesting cultural visits in **Gran Canaria**.

### What to see in Arucas
The city's main symbol is the spectacular **Church of San Juan Bautista**, a neo-Gothic gem built entirely from blue volcanic stone. It's also worth exploring the **Historic Center of Arucas**, visiting the iconic **Arehucas Distillery**, strolling through the well-kept **Municipal Park**, discovering the gardens of the **Marquesa de Arucas** and climbing **Montaña de Arucas**, one of the best viewpoints in northern **Gran Canaria**.

### What to do in Arucas
Walking through the historic streets of **Arucas** lets you admire some of the most elegant buildings on the island. You can also learn about the city's rum-making tradition, visit old farming estates, enjoy local cuisine or hike trails with panoramic views over the north coast. For photography lovers, the municipality offers some of the most beautiful urban corners in **Gran Canaria**.

### Is Arucas worth visiting?
**Without a doubt.** Arucas is one of the most complete municipalities in **Gran Canaria** for those seeking culture, architecture and history. Its impressive heritage, the beauty of its streets and the presence of landmarks such as the **Arucas Cathedral** and the **Arehucas Distillery** make it a must-visit during any trip to the island.

### Tips for your visit
- ⛪ Visit the **Church of San Juan Bautista**, one of the most impressive monuments in the Canary Islands
- 📸 Climb **Montaña de Arucas** to enjoy magnificent panoramic views
- 🥃 Discover the history of rum at the famous **Arehucas Distillery**
- 🌴 Stroll through the historic center and its elegant squares and gardens
- 🍌 Take in the banana plantations that surround much of the municipality
- ☀️ Combine the visit with other towns in northern **Gran Canaria**

### Recommendation
Take a few hours to explore **Arucas** at a relaxed pace. Between its spectacular architecture, its agricultural tradition, its historic gardens and some of the most iconic monuments in **Gran Canaria**, you'll discover one of the islands' most distinctive and charming towns.
municipios.shortDescription: Arucas stands out for its impressive volcanic stone cathedral, the Arehucas Distillery, the Montaña de Arucas and one of the most elegant historic centers in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Firgas
municipios.description:
**Firgas** is one of the most charming villages in northern **Gran Canaria**. Known as the **Villa del Agua** (Water Town), this small midland municipality stands out for its abundant springs, traditional Canarian architecture and one of the most singular promenades on the whole island. Surrounded by green landscapes, ravines and natural viewpoints, **Firgas** offers a calm and authentic experience, perfect for those wanting to discover the most rural and traditional side of **Gran Canaria**.

### What to see in Firgas
The main attraction is the famous **Paseo de Gran Canaria**, decorated with waterfalls, fountains and colorful tiles representing the island's municipalities. It's also worth visiting the historic **center of Firgas**, the **Church of San Roque**, the **Mirador de Las Pellas** and the many corners that preserve traditional Canarian architecture. From various points in the municipality you'll get magnificent views of the north coast and the mountains in the interior of **Gran Canaria**.

### What to do in Firgas
Strolling through its cobbled streets is one of the best ways to discover the character of **Firgas**. You can also enjoy hiking routes around the area, visit small local shops and cafés, learn about the history of water on the island, or follow rural paths connecting the municipality with other towns in the north. Its calm atmosphere makes it an ideal place for a relaxed visit.

### Is Firgas worth visiting?
**Yes.** Although it's one of the smallest municipalities in **Gran Canaria**, it has a unique personality. Its famous promenade, the beauty of its historic center and its natural surroundings make **Firgas** a highly recommended stop for anyone exploring the north of the island.

### Tips for your visit
- 💧 Walk along the famous **Paseo de Gran Canaria**, one of the most photographed spots in the municipality
- 📸 Visit the **Mirador de Las Pellas** for excellent panoramic views
- 👟 Take the chance to walk through the historic streets and discover charming corners
- ☕ Take a break at a local café to enjoy the village's quiet atmosphere
- 🌿 Combine the visit with other nearby municipalities in northern **Gran Canaria**
- 🚗 The municipality is a short distance from **Arucas**, **Moya** and **Teror**

### Recommendation
Take a few hours to explore **Firgas** at a relaxed pace. Between its fountains, traditional streets, viewpoints and the iconic **Paseo de Gran Canaria**, you'll discover one of the most picturesque and authentic villages in the north of the island.
municipios.shortDescription: Firgas, the Water Town of Gran Canaria, stands out for its famous Paseo de Gran Canaria, its historic fountains and the charm of one of the prettiest villages in the north of the island.

municipios.name: Gáldar
municipios.description:
**Gáldar** is one of the municipalities with the greatest historical and cultural value in **Gran Canaria**. Considered the ancient capital of the **guanartemes**, the kings of the ancient Canarians, this town played a fundamental role in the island's pre-Hispanic history. Today it combines important archaeological sites, an attractive historic center, a spectacular volcanic coastline and some of the most deeply rooted traditions in **Gran Canaria**.

### What to see in Gáldar
A must-visit is the **Cueva Pintada Museum and Archaeological Park**, one of the most important sites in the Canary Islands and a unique window into the island's aboriginal past. Also notable are the monumental **Church of Santiago de los Caballeros**, the **Plaza de Santiago**, the historic center of **Gáldar** and various archaeological sites scattered around the municipality. Along the coast, highlights include **Sardina del Norte**, **Playa de El Agujero**, **La Furnia** and the many natural pools formed by volcanic activity.

### What to do in Gáldar
**Gáldar** offers experiences for all tastes. You can learn about the history of the ancient Canarians, stroll through its historic streets, enjoy beaches and natural pools, snorkel in **Sardina del Norte** or hike trails connecting the coast with the midlands of northern **Gran Canaria**. Its combination of heritage, nature and gastronomy makes it one of the most complete municipalities on the island.

### Is Gáldar worth visiting?
**Absolutely.** Few places give such insight into the history of **Gran Canaria** as **Gáldar**. Its archaeological richness, its monumental heritage and the beauty of its coastline make it one of the most recommended visits for anyone wanting to learn about the island's identity and past.

### Tips for your visit
- 🏺 Set aside time to visit the **Cueva Pintada**, one of the most important sites in the Canary Islands
- ⛪ Discover the impressive **Church of Santiago de los Caballeros** and its historic surroundings
- 🌊 Head to **Sardina del Norte** to enjoy the sea and its fishing village atmosphere
- 📸 Explore the volcanic coastline and the municipality's natural pools
- 🍽️ Try the local cuisine at restaurants in the historic center or along the coast
- 🚗 Combine the visit with other northern municipalities such as **Agaete**, **Moya** or **Santa María de Guía**

### Recommendation
Spend at least a day discovering **Gáldar**. Between the **Cueva Pintada**, its historic heritage, its beaches, natural pools and some of the most spectacular coastal landscapes in northern **Gran Canaria**, you'll find one of the most fascinating and complete municipalities on the entire island.
municipios.shortDescription: Gáldar, the ancient capital of the Canarian aborigines, stands out for the Cueva Pintada, its historic heritage and some of the best volcanic coastline in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Ingenio
municipios.description:
**Ingenio** is one of the municipalities that best represents tradition and craftsmanship in **Gran Canaria**. Located in the southeast of the island, it stands out for preserving a strong cultural identity linked to rural life, traditional crops and the famous **calado canario**, a delicate embroidery technique that forms part of the Canary Islands' historic heritage. Its combination of history, nature and local customs makes **Ingenio** an excellent destination for anyone wanting to discover the authentic essence of **Gran Canaria**.

### What to see in Ingenio
The main attraction is the **Historic Center of Ingenio**, where traditional buildings, quiet squares and some of the most charming corners in the southeast of the island are preserved. It's also worth visiting the **Calado Museum**, dedicated to one of the most iconic crafts in the Canary Islands, as well as the **Church of Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria**. In the surrounding area, the agricultural landscapes, ravines and various trails offer a glimpse into the municipality's rural history.

### What to do in Ingenio
**Ingenio** is an ideal place for a relaxed stroll, discovering local crafts and exploring some of the lesser-known landscapes of **Gran Canaria**. Culture lovers can learn about the calado tradition, while nature enthusiasts will find routes through ravines, farmland and natural areas inland. It's also an excellent base for exploring other nearby municipalities in the southeast of the island.

### Is Ingenio worth visiting?
**Yes.** Although it tends to be overlooked compared to other better-known destinations in **Gran Canaria**, Ingenio offers an authentic and different experience. It's especially recommended for travelers interested in local culture, Canarian traditions and towns that preserve their historic identity.

### Tips for your visit
- 🧵 Discover the tradition of **calado canario**, one of the most representative crafts on the island
- 🏛️ Explore the **Historic Center of Ingenio** and its traditional buildings
- ⛪ Visit the **Church of Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria**, one of the municipality's landmarks
- 📸 The nearby rural landscapes and ravines offer excellent photo opportunities
- 🚶 Stroll through the center to experience the town's calm, authentic atmosphere
- 🍽️ Take the chance to try traditional Canarian cuisine at local establishments

### Recommendation
Combine a visit to **Ingenio** with exploring the rural landscapes of southeastern **Gran Canaria** and the nearby **Guayadeque Ravine**. Between tradition, craftsmanship, history and nature, you'll discover one of the most distinctive and authentic municipalities on the island.
municipios.shortDescription: Ingenio stands out for its craft tradition, the famous Canarian calado embroidery, its historic center and the authentic atmosphere of one of the most traditional villages in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: La Aldea de San Nicolás
municipios.description:
**La Aldea de San Nicolás** is one of the most authentic, quiet and least crowded municipalities in Gran Canaria. Located at the western tip of the island and surrounded by some of the most spectacular landscapes in the archipelago, it combines volcanic mountains, deep ravines, extensive farmland and a wild coastline where nature remains the main attraction. Its historic isolation has allowed it to preserve its own identity and a pace of life very different from the tourist areas in the south.

### What to see in La Aldea de San Nicolás
Among its main attractions are the spectacular **Playa de La Aldea**, the historic town center, the viewpoints over the valley and the impressive landscapes surrounding the municipality. Very close by are some of the most iconic spots in western Gran Canaria, such as **Playa de Güigüi**, **Tasartico**, **Tasarte** and the famous **Mirador del Balcón**, one of the best viewpoints in the Canary Islands.

### What to do
La Aldea is an ideal destination for hikers, nature lovers and travelers seeking a different side of Gran Canaria. Some of the island's most spectacular routes start here, including the trail to Güigüi. It's also an excellent starting point for driving the scenic GC-200 road, visiting unspoiled beaches, taking in cliffs over the Atlantic, or exploring unique ravines and volcanic landscapes.

### Is La Aldea worth visiting?
Without a doubt. If you're looking for tourist beaches and large hotel complexes, this probably isn't your main destination. However, for those wanting to discover the most authentic side of Gran Canaria, enjoy spectacular landscapes and get away from the busier areas, La Aldea is one of the most recommended visits on the whole island.

### Tips for your visit
- 🚗 Having a car is highly recommended to explore the area
- ☀️ Bring water and sun protection, especially if you go hiking
- 📸 Sunsets on the west coast are among the best in Gran Canaria
- 🥾 If you plan to visit Güigüi, start the hike early
- 🍅 Take the chance to discover the municipality's agricultural tradition and local produce

### Recommendation
Spend at least a full day exploring La Aldea de San Nicolás. Between mountains, ravines, unspoiled beaches and some of the most impressive landscapes in the Canary Islands, you'll discover one of the most surprising and least-known areas of Gran Canaria.
municipios.shortDescription: La Aldea de San Nicolás combines pristine beaches, hiking, nature and some of the most spectacular and authentic landscapes in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria
municipios.description:
**Las Palmas de Gran Canaria** is the capital of **Gran Canaria** and one of the most fascinating cities in the Atlantic. With more than five centuries of history, it combines internationally famous urban beaches, historic neighborhoods, an intense cultural life and an excellent food scene. Thanks to its privileged climate all year round, its rich heritage and its cosmopolitan atmosphere, it has become one of the most appealing urban destinations in Spain.

### What to see in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria
Must-see spots include the famous **Las Canteras Beach**, considered one of the best urban beaches in Europe, the historic **Vegueta district**, the majestic **Cathedral of Santa Ana**, the **Casa de Colón**, the **Museo Canario** and the iconic **Castillo de la Luz**. It's also worth exploring the **Triana** neighborhood, the marina, **Parque de Santa Catalina** and numerous cultural venues throughout the city.

### What to do in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria
The possibilities are almost endless. You can relax on **Las Canteras Beach**, snorkel along its natural reef, explore centuries of history in **Vegueta**, enjoy museums and exhibitions, go shopping in **Triana** or discover local cuisine in markets and restaurants. The city also offers a packed calendar of cultural events, festivals and activities throughout the year.

### Is Las Palmas de Gran Canaria worth visiting?
**Without a doubt.** Las Palmas de Gran Canaria brings together beach, history, culture, gastronomy and leisure in a single destination. It's a city capable of offering very different experiences within a few kilometers, from walking through 15th-century historic streets to watching the sunset over the Atlantic from the sand of **Las Canteras**.

### Tips for your visit
- 🏖️ Take time to walk the full length of **Las Canteras Beach** and its promenade
- 🏛️ Explore the historic **Vegueta district**, the origin of the city in 1478
- ⛪ Visit the **Cathedral of Santa Ana** and climb its tower for great views
- 🖼️ Discover the history of the Canary Islands at **Casa de Colón** and the **Museo Canario**
- 🍽️ Try local cuisine in markets, terraces and traditional restaurants
- 📸 Sunrise at **Las Canteras** and sunset over the harbor area both make for excellent photos
- 🚶 The city is perfect for exploring on foot between historic neighborhoods and coastal areas

### Recommendation
Set aside at least one or two days to discover **Las Palmas de Gran Canaria**. Between **Las Canteras Beach**, **Vegueta**, its museums, historic monuments, cultural venues and excellent cuisine, you'll find one of the most complete, vibrant and interesting cities in the entire Canarian archipelago.
municipios.shortDescription: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria combines Las Canteras Beach, Vegueta, history, culture and a vibrant urban life in the capital of Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Mogán
municipios.description:
**Mogán** is one of the most visited and sunniest municipalities in **Gran Canaria**. Located at the southwestern tip of the island, it stands out for its spectacular beaches, its impressive volcanic ravines and a privileged climate that has earned it a reputation as one of the best-climate spots in Europe. Thanks to its combination of coastline, nature and tourist amenities, **Mogán** has become one of the most popular destinations in the Canary Islands.

### What to see in Mogán
Must-see spots include the picturesque **Puerto de Mogán**, known as the "Little Venice" of **Gran Canaria**, the famous beaches of **Amadores**, **Puerto Rico**, **Anfi del Mar**, **Tauro** and **Taurito**, as well as the spectacular landscapes of the municipality's interior. Natural spots like **Playa de Güigüi**, **Tasartico**, **Tasarte**, **Veneguera** and the striking **Azulejos de Veneguera**, one of the most eye-catching geological formations on the island, are also worth a visit.

### What to do in Mogán
**Mogán** offers activities for all kinds of travelers. You can relax on some of the best beaches in **Gran Canaria**, practice water sports, take boat trips to spot dolphins and whales, hike trails through volcanic ravines or discover small villages and farming valleys inland. The municipality also has a wide range of dining, shopping and leisure options throughout the year.

### Is Mogán worth visiting?
**Absolutely.** Mogán brings together some of the most famous beaches in **Gran Canaria**, spectacular landscapes and a huge variety of activities. Whether you're looking for relaxation by the sea or prefer hiking, nature or excursions, you'll find options for every taste in one of the island's most complete municipalities.

### Tips for your visit
- 🏖️ Take time to discover several beaches, as each offers a different experience
- 🚤 Dolphin-watching excursions are one of the most popular activities in the municipality
- 📸 Stroll through the charming **Puerto de Mogán**, one of the most photographed spots in **Gran Canaria**
- 🥾 Explore trails toward **Güigüi**, **Tasartico** or the ravines inland
- ☀️ Wear sun protection all year round, even in winter
- 🌅 Sunsets on the southwest coast are considered among the best on the island

### Recommendation
Set aside at least one or two days to discover **Mogán**. Between crystal-clear beaches, charming coastal villages, volcanic ravines and some of the most spectacular landscapes in **Gran Canaria**, you'll find one of the most complete and appealing destinations in the entire archipelago.
municipios.shortDescription: Mogán combines some of the best beaches in Gran Canaria, Puerto de Mogán, spectacular volcanic ravines and some of the most impressive landscapes in the southwest of the island.

municipios.name: Moya
municipios.description:
**Moya** is one of the greenest and most surprising municipalities in **Gran Canaria**. Located in the north of the island, it stands out for its deep ravines, its lush landscapes and for being home to some of the last remnants of the ancient **laurisilva**, the subtropical forest that covered much of the Canary Islands millions of years ago. Its natural surroundings, historic heritage and relaxed atmosphere make **Moya** an ideal destination for those seeking nature and authenticity.

### What to see in Moya
The most iconic spot is undoubtedly **Los Tilos de Moya**, one of the most valuable natural areas in **Gran Canaria** and one of the island's last remaining pockets of laurisilva. It's also worth visiting the historic **center of Moya**, the impressive **Church of Nuestra Señora de Candelaria**, built over a ravine, and the many natural viewpoints offering spectacular views over the north coast and the mountains inland.

### What to do in Moya
**Moya** is a perfect destination for hiking and nature lovers. Its trails wind through humid forests, ravines covered in vegetation and rural landscapes that show a lesser-known side of **Gran Canaria**. You can also discover local cuisine, visit traditional markets and try the famous **suspiros de Moya**, one of the island's most representative sweets.

### Is Moya worth visiting?
**Yes, especially if you love nature.** Moya offers landscapes completely different from the drier, more touristy image many visitors associate with **Gran Canaria**. Its forests, ravines and trails reveal one of the calmest and best-preserved environments on the whole island.

### Tips for your visit
- 🌳 Walk the trail through **Los Tilos de Moya**, one of the most important natural areas in the Canary Islands
- 👟 Wear comfortable footwear to enjoy the municipality's paths and trails
- 📸 The ravines and viewpoints offer excellent opportunities for landscape photography
- 🍰 Try the traditional **suspiros de Moya**, one of the most famous sweets in **Gran Canaria**
- 🌿 Stick to marked trails to help protect the area's ecosystems
- 🌧️ Some routes can be wet or slippery after rain

### Recommendation
Spend a few hours discovering **Moya** and its natural areas. Between **Los Tilos de Moya**, its green landscapes, its historic heritage and some of the prettiest trails in **Gran Canaria**, you'll find one of the most authentic, peaceful and surprising municipalities in the north of the island.
municipios.shortDescription: Moya stands out for Los Tilos de Moya, its laurel forests, green ravines and some of the most spectacular natural landscapes in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: San Bartolomé de Tirajana
municipios.description:
**San Bartolomé de Tirajana** is the largest municipality in **Gran Canaria** and one of the most important tourist destinations in Europe. Its vast territory encompasses some of the most spectacular and diverse landscapes on the island, from the famous **Maspalomas Dunes** and the southern beaches to deep ravines, traditional villages and the mountains inland. This extraordinary variety makes **San Bartolomé de Tirajana** a unique place where nature, leisure, culture and adventure coexist within a single municipality.

### What to see in San Bartolomé de Tirajana
The most iconic spots are the impressive **Maspalomas Dunes**, the **Charca de Maspalomas** lagoon, the historic **Maspalomas Lighthouse** and the extensive beaches of **Maspalomas**, **Playa del Inglés**, **San Agustín** and **Meloneras**. Inland, highlights include natural sites such as the **Fataga Ravine**, the spectacular **Degollada de las Yeguas**, the traditional village of **Fataga** and the impressive **Necrópolis de Arteara**, one of the most important archaeological sites in **Gran Canaria**.

### What to do in San Bartolomé de Tirajana
The options are practically endless. You can relax on some of the best beaches in **Gran Canaria**, walk across the **Maspalomas Dunes**, practice water sports, go hiking through ravines and mountains, or discover small villages full of history and tradition. The municipality also has a wide range of leisure venues, restaurants, shopping centers and activities for all ages throughout the year.

### Is San Bartolomé de Tirajana worth visiting?
**Absolutely.** San Bartolomé de Tirajana is home to many of the most visited and photographed spots in **Gran Canaria**. Its combination of beaches, volcanic landscapes, historic heritage and protected natural areas allows you to enjoy very different experiences without leaving the municipality.

### Tips for your visit
- 🏜️ Walk across the spectacular **Maspalomas Dunes**, one of the most iconic landscapes in the Canary Islands
- 🏖️ Take time to enjoy the beaches of **Maspalomas**, **Playa del Inglés** and **San Agustín**
- 📸 Visit the **Degollada de las Yeguas**, one of the best viewpoints in **Gran Canaria**
- 🥾 Explore the **Fataga Ravine** and the trails inland
- 🏛️ Discover aboriginal history at the **Necrópolis de Arteara**
- ☀️ Wear sun protection all year round, especially on the coast and in the dunes
- 🌅 Watch the sunset by the **Maspalomas Lighthouse**, one of the island's most iconic spots

### Recommendation
Set aside several days to discover **San Bartolomé de Tirajana**. From the famous **Maspalomas Dunes** to the ravines and mountains inland, this municipality brings together some of the most spectacular, varied and representative landscapes in **Gran Canaria**, making it a must-visit for any traveler.
municipios.shortDescription: San Bartolomé de Tirajana brings together the Maspalomas Dunes, Playa del Inglés, Fataga and some of the most spectacular and varied landscapes in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Santa Brígida
municipios.description:
**Santa Brígida** is one of the most elegant and traditional municipalities in **Gran Canaria**. Located in the midlands of the northeast of the island, it stands out for its green landscapes, its historic winemaking tradition and some of the most beautiful corners of the Gran Canaria interior. Thanks to its mild climate, fertile lands and proximity to the capital, **Santa Brígida** has become one of the favorite destinations for those wanting to discover the calmer, rural side of **Gran Canaria**.

### What to see in Santa Brígida
Among the most notable sights are the charming **Historic Center of Santa Brígida**, the famous **Bandama Caldera**, one of the best-preserved volcanic craters in the Canary Islands, and the picturesque **El Madroñal** neighborhood. It's also worth visiting its historic gardens, old estates, traditional wineries and various viewpoints with views over northeastern **Gran Canaria**.

### What to do in Santa Brígida
**Santa Brígida** is an ideal destination for wine tourism, hiking and discovering local cuisine. You can visit family-run wineries, hike trails through vineyards and volcanic landscapes, explore the **Bandama Caldera** or stroll through its quiet streets surrounded by traditional Canarian architecture. Its location also makes it easy to combine the visit with other iconic spots on the island.

### Is Santa Brígida worth visiting?
**Yes, without a doubt.** Santa Brígida offers an experience different from the coastal areas of **Gran Canaria**. It's a perfect destination for those seeking nature, tranquility, gastronomy and some of the most appealing rural landscapes on the island. Its historic importance in wine production and its natural surroundings make it one of the most interesting visits in the Gran Canaria interior.

### Tips for your visit
