- 🍇 Discover the wineries and local wines that have made **Santa Brígida** famous
- 🌋 Visit the impressive **Bandama Caldera**, one of the great natural monuments of **Gran Canaria**
- 📸 The viewpoints and volcanic landscapes offer excellent photo opportunities
- 🚶 Stroll through the historic center and enjoy its calm, traditional atmosphere
- 🍽️ Try the local cuisine at restaurants and rural estates in the area
- ☀️ Wear sun protection if you plan to hike or visit open areas

### Recommendation
Spend a day discovering **Santa Brígida** and its surroundings. Between the **Bandama Caldera**, the vineyards, the historic wineries and some of the most elegant and green landscapes in **Gran Canaria**, you'll find one of the most charming and distinctive municipalities in the island's interior.
municipios.shortDescription: Santa Brígida stands out for the Bandama Caldera, its vineyards, historic wineries and some of the most elegant rural landscapes in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Santa Lucía de Tirajana
municipios.description:
**Santa Lucía de Tirajana** is one of the municipalities with the greatest scenic, historic and cultural richness in **Gran Canaria**. Located in the southeast of the island, its territory stretches from the midlands to the peaks, crossing deep ravines, palm groves and some of the most important settings in Canarian aboriginal history. Thanks to its combination of archaeological heritage, nature and rural traditions, **Santa Lucía de Tirajana** is a must-visit for anyone wanting to discover the most authentic Gran Canaria.

### What to see in Santa Lucía de Tirajana
One of the most iconic sites is the impressive **Fortaleza de Ansite**, considered one of the last strongholds of resistance of the ancient Canarians during the conquest of the island. The charming **Historic Center of Santa Lucía**, the spectacular **Tirajana Ravine**, the **Sorrueda Palm Grove**, the **Sorrueda Reservoir** and various viewpoints offering magnificent panoramas over the interior of **Gran Canaria** are also notable. Very close by are some of the most representative landscapes of the southeastern midlands.

### What to do in Santa Lucía de Tirajana
**Santa Lucía de Tirajana** is an ideal destination for hiking, history and nature lovers. You can walk along old royal paths, visit archaeological sites, discover palm groves and ravines, or enjoy panoramic routes through some of the most spectacular landscapes in **Gran Canaria**. The municipality also retains an important agricultural and culinary tradition that can be discovered in its villages and local markets.

### Is Santa Lucía de Tirajana worth visiting?
**Yes, absolutely.** Santa Lucía offers a different view of **Gran Canaria**, away from the coastal tourist areas. Its enormous historic value, the beauty of its landscapes and the importance of sites like the **Fortaleza de Ansite** make it one of the most interesting municipalities for understanding the island's history and identity.

### Tips for your visit
- 🏰 Visit the historic **Fortaleza de Ansite**, one of the most important sites in the history of the Canary Islands
- 🥾 Walk the trails that cross the **Tirajana Ravine** and the municipality's midlands
- 📸 The viewpoints offer some of the best views of the interior of **Gran Canaria**
- 🌴 Discover the beautiful **Sorrueda Palm Grove** and its natural surroundings
- ☀️ Bring water and sun protection if you plan to hike
- 🍽️ Take the chance to sample traditional cuisine at local restaurants

### Recommendation
Spend a full day exploring **Santa Lucía de Tirajana**. Between the **Fortaleza de Ansite**, the ravines, palm groves, historic trails and volcanic landscapes, you'll discover one of the most authentic, historic and surprising municipalities in **Gran Canaria**.
municipios.shortDescription: Santa Lucía de Tirajana stands out for the Fortaleza de Ansite, its ravines, palm groves and some of the most impressive historic landscapes in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Santa María de Guía de Gran Canaria
municipios.description:
**Santa María de Guía de Gran Canaria**, commonly known as **Guía**, is one of the municipalities with the richest history and culinary tradition in northern **Gran Canaria**. Famous for producing the prestigious **Queso de Flor de Guía**, unique in the world for being made with vegetable rennet, this town combines cultural heritage, rural landscapes, agricultural tradition and some of the most authentic corners on the island. Its privileged location between the coast and the midlands makes it an excellent base for exploring the north of Gran Canaria.

### What to see in Santa María de Guía
The main attraction is the elegant **Historic Center of Guía**, declared a **Site of Cultural Interest**, where the **Iglesia Matriz de Santa María de Guía**, traditional squares and numerous manor houses reflect the municipality's historic importance. It's also worth visiting the nearby **Cenobio de Valerón**, one of the most impressive archaeological sites in the Canary Islands, as well as the rural landscapes and viewpoints surrounding the town.

### What to do in Santa María de Guía
**Guía** is an ideal destination for those wanting to combine culture, gastronomy and nature. You can walk through its historic streets, visit artisan cheese makers, sample local products, explore rural trails or discover some of the most important sites in the aboriginal history of **Gran Canaria**. Its proximity to other northern municipalities also makes it possible to combine several excursions in a single day.

### Is Santa María de Guía worth visiting?
**Without a doubt.** Guía offers an authentic experience that lets you discover the history, traditions and cuisine of **Gran Canaria**. Its famous **Queso de Flor de Guía**, its historic heritage and its proximity to important archaeological sites make it a highly recommended visit for any traveler wanting to discover the island beyond its beaches.

### Tips for your visit
- 🧀 Try the authentic **Queso de Flor de Guía**, one of the most prestigious culinary products in the Canary Islands
- 🏛️ Explore the **Historic Center of Guía** and discover its traditional architecture
- ⛪ Visit the **Iglesia Matriz de Santa María de Guía**, one of the municipality's most iconic buildings
- 🏺 Head to the impressive **Cenobio de Valerón**, one of the great archaeological treasures of **Gran Canaria**
- 📸 The rural landscapes and midlands offer excellent photo opportunities
- 🍽️ Take the chance to discover local cuisine and artisan products from the north of the island

### Recommendation
Spend a few hours discovering **Santa María de Guía de Gran Canaria**. Between its historic heritage, its culinary traditions, the famous **Queso de Flor de Guía** and landmarks such as the **Cenobio de Valerón**, you'll find one of the municipalities with the most history, identity and flavor in **Gran Canaria**.
municipios.shortDescription: Santa María de Guía stands out for the famous Queso de Flor de Guía cheese, its historic center and the Cenobio de Valerón, one of the most important archaeological sites in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Tejeda
municipios.description:
**Tejeda** is considered one of the most beautiful villages in **Gran Canaria** and one of the most spectacular destinations in the entire Canarian archipelago. Located in the mountainous heart of the island and surrounded by some of the most iconic landscapes in the Canary Islands, this municipality offers a unique combination of nature, history, gastronomy and tradition. Its impressive panoramas over **Roque Nublo**, **Roque Bentayga** and the **Tejeda Caldera** make it a must-visit for any traveler.

### What to see in Tejeda
The main stars are the majestic **Roque Nublo** and the historic **Roque Bentayga**, two of the most important natural symbols of **Gran Canaria**. The charming **Historic Center of Tejeda**, the spectacular **Tejeda Caldera**, the **Mirador de Unamuno** and numerous viewpoints scattered across the peaks are also notable. The municipality is also part of the cultural landscape of **Risco Caído and the Sacred Mountains of Gran Canaria**, declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

### What to do in Tejeda
**Tejeda** is one of the best destinations in **Gran Canaria** for hiking, enjoying panoramic routes and discovering unique volcanic landscapes. You can walk trails leading to **Roque Nublo**, visit **Roque Bentayga**, explore viewpoints with spectacular views, or simply stroll through one of the prettiest villages in Spain. Food lovers will also find some of the island's most famous sweets here, made with local almonds.

### Is Tejeda worth visiting?
**Absolutely.** For many travelers, **Tejeda** represents the most authentic essence of **Gran Canaria**. Its combination of mountains, history, nature and culture offers a completely different experience from the coastal areas. The views from its viewpoints are considered among the best in the whole of the Canary Islands.

### Tips for your visit
- 📸 Visit the **Mirador de Unamuno**, one of the most impressive natural balconies on the island
- 🥾 Walk the trail to **Roque Nublo**, one of the most popular routes in **Gran Canaria**
- 🏛️ Discover aboriginal history around **Roque Bentayga**
- 🌸 If you visit between January and February, enjoy the spectacular **almond blossom**
- 🍰 Try the famous sweets and marzipan made with **Tejeda** almonds
- 🧥 Bring something warm, especially during winter months or at sunset
- 🌅 Sunrise and sunset offer some of the best views in **Gran Canaria**

### Recommendation
Spend a full day discovering **Tejeda** and its surroundings. Between **Roque Nublo**, **Roque Bentayga**, the **Tejeda Caldera**, its trails and its impressive viewpoints, you'll find some of the most spectacular and representative landscapes in **Gran Canaria**.
municipios.shortDescription: Tejeda combines Roque Nublo, Roque Bentayga, spectacular mountain landscapes and one of the prettiest villages in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Telde
municipios.description:
**Telde** is the second most populous city in **Gran Canaria** and one of the municipalities with the greatest historic importance on the island. Considered one of the ancient kingdoms of the Canarian aborigines before the conquest, it combines valuable cultural heritage, beautiful beaches, archaeological sites and a vibrant local life. Thanks to its strategic location between the capital and the touristy south, **Telde** has become one of the most interesting places to discover the authentic essence of **Gran Canaria**.

### What to see in Telde
The main attraction is the historic **San Juan neighborhood**, declared a **Site of Cultural Interest**, where the impressive **Basilica of San Juan Bautista** stands out, known for housing important works of religious art. It's also worth visiting the historic **San Francisco** neighborhood, the traditional squares of the center, the **Cuatro Puertas** archaeological site, and some of the municipality's most popular coastal spots, such as **Melenara**, **La Garita**, **Tufia** and **Salinetas**.

### What to do in Telde
**Telde** offers activities for all kinds of visitors. You can walk through its historic streets, learn about the legacy of the ancient Canarians, relax on its beaches, snorkel along the east coast or enjoy local cuisine at the many restaurants by the sea. Its natural areas, ravines and trails also reveal a lesser-known side of **Gran Canaria**.

### Is Telde worth visiting?
**Yes, without a doubt.** Telde brings together history, culture, archaeology and coastline in a single municipality. Its rich heritage and the variety of experiences it offers make it one of the most complete visits in **Gran Canaria**, especially for those wanting to combine beach and historic heritage in the same day.

### Tips for your visit
- ⛪ Visit the historic **Basilica of San Juan Bautista**, one of the most important churches in **Gran Canaria**
- 🏛️ Stroll through the historic **San Juan** and **San Francisco** neighborhoods
- 🏺 Discover the **Cuatro Puertas** archaeological site, one of the most important on the island
- 🌊 Head to beaches like **Melenara**, **La Garita** or **Tufia** to enjoy Telde's coastline
- 📸 The historic center offers some of the best urban photo opportunities in **Gran Canaria**
- 🍽️ Try the fresh fish and local cuisine at the coastal restaurants
- ☀️ Combine a cultural visit with a beach afternoon to make the most of the municipality

### Recommendation
Spend at least a day discovering **Telde**. Between its impressive historic heritage, its archaeological sites, its beaches and some of the most authentic corners of **Gran Canaria**, you'll find one of the most complete and interesting municipalities on the whole island.
municipios.shortDescription: Telde combines significant historic heritage, the Basilica of San Juan Bautista, beaches like Melenara and some of the most notable archaeological sites in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Teror
municipios.description:
**Teror** is one of the most iconic, visited and beloved villages in **Gran Canaria**. Located in the green midlands of the north of the island, it stands out for its extraordinary historic heritage, its traditional wooden balconies and for being home to the **Basilica of Nuestra Señora del Pino**, the sanctuary of the patron saint of **Gran Canaria**. Its calm atmosphere, cultural richness and religious importance make **Teror** an essential stop for anyone wanting to learn about the most authentic traditions of the Canary Islands.

### What to see in Teror
The main attraction is the impressive **Basilica of Nuestra Señora del Pino**, one of the most important places of pilgrimage in the Canary Islands. It's also worth exploring the beautiful **Historic Center of Teror**, famous for its carved wooden Canarian balconies, its cobbled streets and its elegant manor houses. Other notable spots include the **Plaza del Pino**, the old convents and the many shops selling crafts and local food products throughout the center of the municipality.

### What to do in Teror
**Teror** is perfect for a relaxed stroll through one of the most charming villages in **Gran Canaria**. You can visit the basilica, discover traditional Canarian architecture, walk trails through the midlands or enjoy the famous Sunday market, considered one of the most popular on the island. It's also a great place to try local specialties such as the well-known **chorizo de Teror** and other artisan foods.

### Is Teror worth visiting?
**Absolutely.** Teror is one of the most distinctive municipalities in **Gran Canaria** and a must-visit for anyone wanting to discover Canarian history, culture and traditions. Its architectural and religious heritage make it one of the prettiest and most representative villages on the whole island.

### Tips for your visit
- 🕊️ Visit the **Basilica of Nuestra Señora del Pino**, one of the most important churches in the Canary Islands
- 📸 Walk through the historic streets and photograph **Teror's** famous traditional balconies
- 🏛️ Stroll through the **Plaza del Pino**, the historic and social heart of the municipality
- 🛍️ If you visit on a Sunday, take the chance to explore its popular traditional market
- 🌭 Try the famous **chorizo de Teror**, one of the best-known culinary products in **Gran Canaria**
- 🚶 Explore the trails and natural landscapes of the midlands surrounding the municipality
- 🌿 Combine the visit with nearby villages such as **Firgas**, **Arucas** or **Moya**

### Recommendation
Spend at least half a day discovering **Teror**. Between the **Basilica del Pino**, its historic balconies, its traditional atmosphere and some of the most deeply rooted customs in **Gran Canaria**, you'll find one of the most authentic, beautiful and representative villages on the whole island.
municipios.shortDescription: Teror stands out for the Basilica del Pino, its famous Canarian balconies, its traditional market and one of the prettiest historic centers in Gran Canaria.

municipios.name: Valleseco
municipios.description:
**Valleseco** is one of the greenest and most peaceful municipalities in **Gran Canaria**. Located in the midlands of the north of the island, this small village is surrounded by lush forests, pine groves, ravines and rural landscapes that show a side of **Gran Canaria** very different from the sunnier, coastal image it's known for. Its privileged natural surroundings and relaxed atmosphere make it an ideal destination for nature and hiking lovers.

### What to see in Valleseco
